transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this cross-functional check to finalize the production and shipment plan for the customer order of 3,600 pump modules — 600 sterile and 3,000 standard. As you know, Assembly Cell 2 is down due to an electrical fault, so we're working with Cells 1 and 4 only, and the customer requires shipment in the upcoming Sunday-Monday window. Before I lock the schedule, I need input from each of you: process engineering on cell capabilities and cycle times for both module types, quality systems on any inspection or validation requirements especially for the sterile units, workforce coordination on staffing availability across the remaining cells, and logistics on the shipping cutoff and any pickup constraints. Let's go around the table.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag two important constraints on Cell 4 from my commissioning review, which I completed this morning but hasn't yet been entered into the production schedule. First, Cell 4's newly installed fixture requires exactly 2 hours of setup verification before it can be used. Second, Cell 4 is approved for no more than 1,200 modules during this campaign. So Cell 4 cannot handle more than 1,200 units total, and we need to account for that 2-hour setup verification in the timeline.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical quality requirement from the current customer control plan, which I confirmed via the customer portal yesterday. All 600 sterile-pump modules must run on Cell 1 and receive a 100 percent pressure test before packing. This is because Cell 4 has no compatible pressure tester. I want to note that the local work-order file still shows the ordinary inspection route, so it hasn't been updated yet — but the binding requirement is the revised plan from the customer portal, and it mandates Cell 1 exclusively for the sterile units with full pressure testing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my Sunday roster findings. I verified with supervisors this afternoon that the qualified staffing requirement is exactly 4 operators for Cell 1 and exactly 5 operators for Cell 4 — and those are the only qualified operators available for this order. I haven't yet attached this roster to Elena's draft schedule, so everyone should be aware of these staffing numbers as we finalize the plan.

transcript.text: I need to share my carrier confirmations, which I received by email today but haven't yet copied into the shipment plan. I have reserved capacity for exactly 2,400 modules from Dock 2 by Sunday at 18:00 and exactly 1,200 modules from Dock 2 by Monday at 08:00. So the shipping cutoffs are: 2,400 modules must be ready and at Dock 2 by Sunday 18:00, and the remaining 1,200 modules must be ready and at Dock 2 by Monday 08:00. Both pickups are from Dock 2.
